VASSAL.build.module.RandomTextButton.faces: Multiple hits can be applied in one command via the Attacker and Target markers.,In an opposed game\, players can apply hits and other combat commands without selecting the piece. See the Shortcuts help sheet [F1].,Players may draw their initial hands as multiple cards in one go. Check out the Draw Cards buttons to the right of each Player Hand toolbar.,Special game counters may be drawn from the Markers palette [hotkey: F4] to form a stock on the player's side of the board. Counter stocks each have a right-click menu to draw or add counters.,Mother Russia: Drag a "Paper-Strength" counter onto a Russian FA\, LN or LT unit to upgrade that unit. Right-click menu commands allow the counter to be converted to a Cossack or Fieldworks piece instead.,Press F1 to pull up the charts window. One of the charts lists the module's hotkeys and command shortcuts.,Press Escape to show or hide your hand window.,Simply press the Squaring button in your hand window to put your targeted infantry unit into square. For Battalion Mass\, click on your side's count of Battalion Mass markers.,Player Command Size and Tactician hand size are displayed on the Wellington and Napoleon icons to the left of the board.,Ctrl+Shift+H will eliminate your unit in the current combat.,Left-click on a counter store to draw a counter (counter will play\, if applicable). May be disabled in Preferences...Game Options.,Hidden hotkeys Alt+Q and Alt+T will generate another Napoleon quote and module tip respectively.,Several features can be tailored to your needs via Preferences...Game Options tab.,Sound is optional and can be turned on or off for this module on the Preferences...Sounds tab.,Combat markers can be placed by drag and drop as well as by using the right-click menu or left-click on a piece.,The player hands include a set of toolbar menus to facilitate end turn.,The Help toolbar menu lists several useful resources for playing the game and using this module.,Zoom the current map in or out using Hotkeys Ctrl+[ and Ctrl+]. To quickly adjust a map window to your monitor\, try the "fit" options under the magnifying glass toolbar button.,You can claim or give up a Victory Banner by left-clicking on the banner track or Victory Banner.,Game clocks can be enabled to keep approximate track of each side's playing time. F8 will pause clocks. Clicking on a clock will switch the timer over (normally automatic).,To detach a leader without marking the unit\, right-click on the leader piece and select the special command "Detach Leader" (shortcut: Alt+D).,Use left-arrow to access a unit and its right-click menu beneath an attached leader.,After playing a card\, left-click on a unit or its attached leader will order that unit. Double-click an ordered unit or attached leader to proceed to the combat phase. [Preferences...Game Options: Battlefield Click Actions],In the combat phase\, a single left-click on a unit or leader (double-click on an attached leader) will place a combat marker. [Preferences...Game Options: Battlefield Click Actions],For best effect\, apply hits\, Leader Check and retreats in sequence per rules and use the combat marker "Take Hits" menu or equivalent key commands.
VASSAL.build.module.RandomTextButton.name: Module Tips

VASSAL.build.module.RandomTextButton.faces: Sometimes a single battle decides everything and sometimes\, too\, the slightest circumstance decides the issue of a battle.,Doctors will have more lives to answer for in the next world than even we generals.,I love a brave soldier who has undergone the baptism of fire.,If you had seen one day of war\, you would pray to God that you would never see another.,In war\, as in politics\, no evil - even if it is permissible under the rules - is excusable unless it is absolutely necessary. Everything beyond that is a crime.,In war\, morale factors acount for three quarters of the whole; relative material strength accounts for only one quarter.,Remember \, gentlemen\, what a Roman emperor said: The corpse of an enemy always smells sweet.,There is a moment in every battle at which the least manoeuvre is decisive and gives superiority\, as one drop of water causes overflow.,An army marches on its stomach.,An army's effectiveness depends on its size\, training\, experience\, and morale\, and morale is worth more than any of the other factors combined.,Between a battle lost and a battle won\, the distance is immense and there stand empires.,Courage is like love: it must have hope for nourishment.,Every soldier carries a marshal's baton in his pack.,God is on the side with the best artillery,He that makes war without many mistakes has not made war very long.,How many things apparently impossible have nevertheless been performed by resolute men who had no alternative but death.,I have made all the calculations\, fate will do the rest.,If the art of war were nothing but the art of avoiding risks\, glory would become the prey of mediocre minds.,If they want peace\, nations should avoid the pin-pricks that precede cannonshots.,If you wage war\, do it energetically and with severity. This is the only way to make it shorter and consequently less inhuman.,In time of revolution\, with perseverance and courage\, a soldier should think nothing impossible.,In war there is but one favorable moment; the great art is to seize it!,In war\, three-quarters turns on personal character and relations; the balance of manpower and materials counts only for the remaining quarter.,It should not be believed that a march of three or four days in the wrong direction can be corrected by a countermarch. As a rule\, this is to make two mistakes instead of one.,One bad general is worth two good ones.,Read over and over the campaigns of Alexander\, Hannibal\, Caesar\, Gustavus\, Turenne\, Eugene and Frederic. This is the only way to become a great general and master the secrets of the art of war.,Soldiers generally win battles; generals get credit for them.,Strategy is the art of making use of time and space. I am less concerned about the later than the former. Space we can recover\, lost time never.,The basic principle that we must follow in directing the armies of the Republic is this: that they must feed themselves on war at the expense of the enemy territory.,The morale is to the physical as three to one.,The most important qualification of a soldier is fortitude under fatigue and privation. Courage is only second; hardship\, poverty and want are the best school for a soldier.,The secret of war lies in the communications.,There are certain things in war of which the commander alone comprehends the importance. Nothing but his superior firmness and ability can subdue and surmount all difficulties.,There are in Europe many good generals\, but they see too many things at once. I see one thing\, namely the enemy's main body. I try to crush it\, confident that secondary matters will then settle themselves.,There are only two forces in the world\, the sword and the spirit. In the long run the sword will always be conquered by the spirit.,Once I have made up my mind\, everything is forgotten except what leads to success.,There is no man more pusillanimous than I when I am planning a campaign. I purposely exaggerate all the dangers and all the calamities that the circumstances make possible.,To have good soldiers\, a nation must always be at war.,Two armies are two bodies which meet and try to frighten each other.,Victory belongs to the most persevering.,What my enemies call a general peace is my destruction. What I call peace is merely the disarmament of my enemies. Am I not more moderate than they?,You do not get peace by shouting: Peace. Peace is a meaningless word; what we need is a glorious peace.,You must not fight too often with one enemy\, or you will teach him all your art of war.,A general-in-chief should ask\, What should I do if the enemy appeared now in my front\, or on my right\, or on my left?,A rapid march increases all the chances of victory.,When an army is inferior in number\, in cavalry and in artillery\, it is essential to avoid a general action.,If you want to avoid a battle with a superior army\, occupy a good defensive position.,The transition from defensive to offensive is one of the most delicate operations in war.,As far as possible\, the artillery should cover and command the surrounding country.,When you are resolved to fight a battle\, collect your whole force. A single battalion sometimes decides the day.,When you determine to risk a battle\, reserve to yourself every possible chance of success\, more particularly\, if you have to deal with an adversary of superior talent.,Never leave gaps for the enemy to penetrate\, unless it be to draw him into a snare.,Encampments of the same army should be formed so as to protect each other.,Infantry\, cavalry and artillery are nothing without each other.,It is the business of cavalry to follow up the victory\, and to prevent the beaten army from rallying.,Artillery is more essential to cavalry than to infantry\, because cavalry has no fire for its defence.,Artillery should always be placed in the most advantageous positions\, and as far in front of the line of cavalry and infantry\, without comprising the safety of the guns\, as possible.,It depends on the general alone to conquer difficulties by superior talent and resolution.,The science of strategy is only to be acquired by experience\, and by studying the campaigns of all the great captains.,Once the offensive has been assumed\, it must be sustained to the last.,To advance or not to advance is a matter for grave consideration.,Even in offensive warfare in the open field the great secret consists in defensive combats\, and in obliging the enemy to attack.,It is an approved maxim in war\, never to do what the enemy wishes you to do. ,Nothing is so important in war as an undivided command.,Never interrupt your enemy when he is making a mistake.,The battlefield is a scene of constant chaos. The winner will be the one who controls that chaos\, both his own and the enemy’s.,Give me lucky generals.
